purpose: THE authoritative comparable pair for the strict R5 formal gate (plan(20260930-061557).md §8 / task-3). This file is the ONE place the pair is pinned. scripts/e4/r5-real-formal.mjs, scripts/e4/r97-observe-arms.mjs, apps/cli/src/r5-formal-gate.test.ts and CI all read it, so a pair change is a ONE-file change and can never be half-applied.
whyThisPairExists: TWO earlier pairs were audited and rejected in this same file, and the reasons are kept because both are still true. (1) The R87/R92-era pair (4f8d98ec… / 2314ce1d…) PREDATES R0/S1: neither arm carries apps/cli/src/r97-arm-abi.ts (verified with `git rev-parse <sha>:apps/cli/src/r97-arm-abi.ts`), so the formal worker boundary refuses both arms with ARM_WORKER_ABI_UNSUPPORTED BEFORE the first model request. It remains the R97/R101 closed-loop pair and is deliberately untouched. (2) The pair this file pinned next (baseline 6d609208… / candidate 66082ded…) was correct in intent but its baseline is NOT in this repository and cannot be fetched here (git to GitHub is unreachable; `git cat-file -t 6d609208…` -> 'Not a valid object name'), while the file and the report both claimed `--setup-pair` created it locally — that flag was parsed and consumed by NOTHING. (3) The pair below is pinned only after all of N1–N4 and the two N5 blockers were committed, so BOTH arms carry the SAME budget / cancellation / evidence / dispatch-journal infrastructure; the ONLY difference is the pre-registered guidance. Its baseline is DERIVED, never fetched.

baseline.role: comparable baseline: the candidate plus ONE commit whose entire diff is packages/evaluation/src/mechanism-guidance.ts, where TOOL_CALL_EFFICIENCY_GUIDANCE_V1 is neutralised to the empty string. It deliberately fails its own product-strategy assertions; that is the point of a comparable baseline and MUST NOT be 'fixed' on product main.
baseline.branchNote: NOT an ancestor of product main, and not required to be: it is not fetched from anywhere. It is DERIVED deterministically from the candidate by `node scripts/e4/r5-real-formal.mjs --setup-pair` (fixed message, fixed author, fixed timestamp, one reviewed transformation, the commit object written byte-by-byte with `git hash-object -t commit -w --stdin`), so `--setup-pair` reproduces this exact SHA on any machine with the candidate and NO network. `--setup-pair` FAILS CLOSED with BASELINE_PIN_MISMATCH if the derived SHA is not this one.

candidate.role: product main at the pin: carries the real tool_call_efficiency_v1 guidance text AND the shared S1/S2/N1/N2/N3/N4 infrastructure. This is the N5 infrastructure commit; the driver that RUNS the pair is its child commit, which adds only this file and the evidence document.
candidate.mechanism: tool_call_efficiency_v1 guidance ACTIVE (real v2 strategy text)

comparisonScope.sharedBase: Both arms are the same tree except for one file. The candidate IS the baseline's parent, so every other byte is identical: the durable tool budget and its RPC (S1/F1), the cancellation and termination paths (S2/N1), the single-flight slot release (N5-BLOCKER, commit 8ee372a1), the offline identity and script cursor (N2), the pricing guard (N4) and the tool-dispatch journal (N3).
comparisonScope.onlyDifference: packages/evaluation/src/mechanism-guidance.ts — verified with `git diff --name-only <baseline> <candidate>` (exactly one path) and `git diff --numstat` (`1 20`, i.e. the 19-line v2 strategy array replaced by one empty-string assignment).
comparisonScope.attributionRule: Any measured difference between the two arms is attributable to that ONE dimension. A difference in shared infrastructure is NOT a candidate effect; if the arms ever differ anywhere else, the pair is invalid and `allowedArmDiff` will say so.
comparisonScope.whatIsNotClaimed: This pair is a COMPARABLE pair, not a result. The formal campaign's statistical decision on it is INCONCLUSIVE-or-worse by design here (the provider is an offline scripted double), and no champion promotion or model-quality claim may be derived from it.
comparisonScope.closureAndProbe: A one-file guidance change MOVES both the execution-closure digest (packages/evaluation/dist/index.js re-exports ./mechanism-guidance.js) and the R97_ARM_PROBE wiring hash (the probe covers the model-visible system prompt, which contains the guidance text), while the LOADED ENTRY sha256 is IDENTICAL between the arms (the entry reaches the guidance through a bare specifier). Measured on real builds of 2314ce1d vs 4f8d98ec: closure 3a965f7e… vs 3e4cc86e…, entry 55981a62… on BOTH, probe wiring 45af5816… vs 5fe66d91…. Consequence for the gate: `entrySha256` identifies the ENTRY FILE, not the arm build, so the 'exchange the two arms' tamper is caught by `buildDigest`/`probe`, never by the entry hash.

isolation.limitation: trusted-build/no-os-network-sandbox says the MODEL TRANSPORT is not billed and that the two arms are real clean git checkouts at a 40-hex HEAD with differing execution closures. It grants NO OS network isolation to arbitrary arm code: the arm process is NOT network-sandboxed, and that field is kept honest rather than upgraded by this gate.

numbering.note: The plan numbers the r5-real-formal.mjs exit-code defect F5 and the readiness-classification defect F6 (F6 already fixed and committed as 66082de by the readiness owner). The task BOARD's task-2 subject line calls its own legacy-price defect 'F6'; that is a different defect and a different numbering. Every F-number in docs/evidence/E4-R5-report.md uses the PLAN's numbering, and the report states so. The N5-blocker fixed in commit 8ee372a1 (the driver's single-flight slot outliving its request) is NOT one of F30-1..F30-7; it became reachable only when a REAL arm build first ran a real case.
